# Vendored dependency guidance

These dependencies are selected by the root [Cargo patches](../Cargo.toml) and pinned through `Cargo.lock`. Read the affected patch note and the consuming [app](../crates/app/AGENTS.md) or [preview](../crates/preview/AGENTS.md) guide before editing or reviewing. The patch notes record upstream provenance, modified files and removal conditions; keep them current with the local change.

Keep product behavior in the app or preview adapter when the upstream API can express it. A vendor change should identify the missing upstream behavior, its consuming path and the smallest patch that supplies it. Preserve license notices, recorded source provenance and the matching toolkit dependency set. Keep runtime changes distinct from test-only dependencies and fixture changes in the patch note. On an upstream update, compare each local patch with the replacement and retire it only when the consuming behavior remains covered. Remove paired input patches together when upstream supplies both sides.

These packages are excluded workspace members. Workspace checks compile the used dependency code, but do not run every vendored package's own tests. Run a vendored crate's own library tests with [`scripts/vendor-crate-test.sh`](../scripts/vendor-crate-test.sh) `vendor/<crate> [filter...]`, never with `cargo test` in its directory: it builds a copy under `.local/`, made a workspace root of its own, against the root manifest's other patches (single-line `name = { path = "..." }` entries under a plainly written `[patch.crates-io]` header, resolving inside `vendor/`; any other patch form, a quoted or spaced spelling of that header and any header or key with an escape sequence stop the run) and the workspace's `Cargo.lock`, lays it out as its upstream repository does (the other vendored crates of the same upstream revision at the paths their `.cargo_vcs_info.json` gives, and the files of the crate's own `upstream-files/` at their repository paths) so tests that include files from beside their crate build, lists every package it resolves beyond that lock (the crate's dev-dependencies, and any locked version the copy's requirements no longer accept, since cargo keeps one only while it still satisfies them), refuses a registry copy of anything the workspace takes from a path, and builds in `.local/target-vendor`. The `gpui-base` popup-frame patch reaches the kit's `Popover` and the dropdown menus built on it; kit `Select`, `Combobox` and `DatePicker` popovers and tooltips still place themselves from bounds their trigger recorded in an earlier frame, and no app view uses the three dropdowns today. Use the consuming app's rendered-node/input/control regressions for toolkit behavior, its Linux-only `native_accessibility::atspi_state_tests` for the AT-SPI adapter, the macOS patch note's `frame_demand_probe` for dispatch lifetime changes, and preview Mermaid/SVG fixtures for renderer integration. Follow root combined Rust checks after integration; native presentation, focus and resource claims still require the affected native workflow and build identity. Do not run upstream CLI/filesystem examples to validate GitTurtle's passive preview path.

Patch-note or instruction-only changes need reference and diff checks without rebuilding the application.
